---
title: "Gaussian random-intercept ML verification record"
---

The [executed comparison](../notebooks/lmm-verification.qmd) fits identical
observations in R lme4 ML, Python statsmodels MixedLM ML and PHP fit_mixed_intercept.
The [saved report](lmm-results.json) records versions, full outputs, Python
warnings/backend, covariance convention and differences from R.

Six saved R fixtures cover simulated schools with correlated predictors,
a single predictor, no fixed intercept, intercept only, a singleton group and
an exact zero-group-variance boundary. Three-way verification adds missingness
in predictors, outcomes and group IDs. Independent Rust tests also check a
balanced intercept-only sample with analytically known variances and shrinkage.
The deterministic tests run without R/Python installed.

Four additional published datasets—sleepstudy, Orthodont, Machines and Hsb82—
are checked against **both lme4 and nlme saved ML outputs** in Rust and PHP.
The [published-data notebook](../notebooks/lmm-public-verification.qmd) executes
fresh fits in both R packages, statsmodels and PHP and checks every row.
See [source provenance](../data/lmm/index.qmd),
`tests/fixtures/lmm-public-r.json` and the [live report](lmm-public-results.json).
Published-data tolerances retain 1e-7 absolute + 1e-6 relative for ordinary
quantities, use 1e-6 absolute + 1e-6 relative for observation-length outputs, and
1e-7 absolute + 1e-10 relative for likelihood/AIC. The notebook documents the
measured R optimizer precision limit for near-zero Hsb82 residuals. A separate
native-versus-statsmodels check keeps the strict original uniform tolerance.

All fixed-effect inference, covariance, population/conditional fitted values,
both residual definitions, group effects, variances, ICC, marginal likelihood
and AIC are compared at 1e-7 + 1e-6 × abs(reference). Labels/order and missing
positions are exact. Python uses statsmodels estimates with plug-in GLS covariance
to match lme4; its native joint-Hessian covariance is a different convention.
The boundary fixture's Python reference is explicitly the NumPy OLS ML limit,
not a statsmodels mixed optimizer result.

PHP tests check integer/string group identity, null group deletion, invalid
float/boolean labels before deletion, missing warnings and strict rejection.
Rust tests check units, row/group order, invalid shapes, unidentified grouping,
rank deficiency, perfect fits and unsupported zero-residual-variance limits.
An independent observation-level GLS test checks the cached QR reduction at
several variance ratios, with correlated predictors and large outcome offsets;
it verifies both optimized and arbitrary-coefficient residual norms.
The profile search has a finite log-ratio range/grid and is not an exhaustive
global optimization proof. The first model has no REML, random slopes, multiple
grouping factors, finite-sample df adjustments or variance-component tests.
Normal inference with few groups can be unreliable.

```sh
export PHP=/opt/homebrew/bin/php
export PHP_CONFIG=/opt/homebrew/bin/php-config
cargo test --workspace --locked
cargo build -p phit --locked
php -n -d "extension=$PWD/target/debug/libphit.dylib" tests/lmm.php
.context/notebooks-venv/bin/python docs/verifications/compare_lmm.py
QUARTO_PYTHON="$PWD/.context/notebooks-venv/bin/python" quarto render docs/notebooks/lmm-verification.qmd
```

For the published comparisons, run the same command with `--public`. Regenerate
public expectations from the pinned snapshots with
`.context/notebooks-venv/bin/python tests/generate-lmm-public-fixtures.py`;
add `--export` only when intentionally refreshing upstream data.

Use matching PHP tools and `.so` on Linux. Regenerate intentionally with
`Rscript tests/generate-lmm-fixtures.R`; lme4 is a development dependency.
See the [contract](../reference-models.qmd#gaussian-random-intercept-mixed-model),
[math](../notebooks/lmm-math.qmd) and [benchmark](../benchmarks/lmm.qmd).
Linux/PHP-FPM and broader mixed-model structures are not established by this evidence.
